# IrradianceVolume

- Inherits [`Instance`](instance.md)
- Created with `Instance.new("IrradianceVolume")`

Adds bounced light to an area: the light a surface receives from other surfaces instead of directly from a light, such as from a sunlit wall or a red carpet. Parent it to a part: the part's box is the volume. The bounced light is computed at points `Spacing` apart inside the box and applied to everything drawn there, moving or not.

Use one volume per room. A surface uses the volume whose box contains the point just in front of it, so each side of a wall between two rooms is lit by its own room's volume. One volume stretched over two rooms lets light from the bright one leak into the dark one.

The light is computed on the CPU by casting rays against anchored objects, behind the loading screen when a scene opens. It is visual only: each machine computes its own. A machine whose `GraphicsService.GlobalIllumination` is below `High` computes none.

This page lists the members this class declares. Inherited members are
listed on the page of the class that declares them.

## Properties

| Name | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Baked` | `Content` | — | read/write | A file that holds this volume's computed light, as an `asset://` path ending in `.irradiance`. Write it with the editor's Bake command on the volume, or with `engine-host <project> --bake-irradiance`. A machine that computes volumes loads the file instead of casting rays, so the room is lit from the first frame.<br><br>A machine that computes none (`GlobalIllumination` below `High`, such as a phone) reads one color from the file, the average of the whole volume, and lights the box with it in place of the flat ambient light. That gives the room its overall tone at no cost per frame.<br><br>The file is valid only for the volume it was baked for. If the box, `Spacing`, `Bounces` or `Mode` differ, the file is rejected with one logged message and the volume is computed as if it had no file. With `Dynamic` on, the file provides the first light and the volume is computed again as the lighting changes. `Refresh` computes it by rays. The file is not used with `FollowsCamera`.<br><br>Bake again after changing the room. The editor and development runs log a message once when the objects in the box differ from those it was baked with. |
| `Blend` | `number` | `1` | read/write | The distance, in meters, over which the volume fades out beyond the faces of its box, where no other volume applies. |
| `Bounces` | `number` | `1` | read/write | How many times light bounces, from 1 to 3. Each bounce costs as much to compute as the first. |
| `Dynamic` | `boolean` | — | read/write | Whether the volume is computed again when the lighting changes, such as when the sun moves or a light that reaches its box is switched on. The work is spread over several frames, and the picture changes from the old light to the new once the new is complete. When it is off, the volume is computed once and again on `Refresh`. |
| `Enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | read/write | Whether the volume applies. |
| `FollowsCamera` | `boolean` | — | read/write | Whether the volume moves with the camera, to provide bounced light outdoors, where no box can enclose the area. The part then gives only the volume's size; its position is ignored.<br><br>The volume is centered on the camera on a grid of its own cells and follows it a few cells at a time. Points that are in both the old and the new position keep their light, so a move costs only the new points. A room's own volume still applies inside the room; this one lights what no other volume covers. |
| `Intensity` | `number` | `1` | read/write | A multiplier on the volume's light. At 1, the default, the room is as bright as its lights, openings and surfaces make it. Other values are an artistic adjustment. |
| `Levels` | `number` | `1` | read/write | With `FollowsCamera`: the number of nested levels, from 1 to 3. Each level after the first is twice as large around the same center, with points twice as far apart, so light is detailed near the camera and coarse far from it. A part of 40 by 16 by 40 at a `Spacing` of 2 with three levels lights 80 meters in every direction. |
| `Mode` | `Enum.IrradianceMode` | `Enum.IrradianceMode.Full` | read/write | What light the volume provides. `Full` provides the light of the sky and all bounced light, replacing the sky's light and `Lighting.Ambient`. `BounceOnly` provides only bounced light, added to them. Changing it computes the volume again. |
| `Spacing` | `number` | `2` | read/write | The distance between the volume's points, in meters, along each side of the box. The minimum is 0.5.<br><br>A box that needs more than 4,096 points, or more than 32 along a side, is computed as up to sixteen tiles that blend where they meet; the eight nearest the camera are drawn. A box that would need more tiles than that is given a coarser spacing, and a message is logged once. |
| `Tint` | `Color3` | `Color3.new(1, 1, 1)` | read/write | A color the volume's light is multiplied by. It can change every frame at no cost; nothing is computed again. |

## Methods

### `GetProgress(): number`

Returns how much of the computation is done, from 0 to 1. Use it for a loading screen. It is 1 when the volume's own light is being drawn, and also on a machine that computes none. It stays 1 while a `Dynamic` volume is being computed again after the lighting changed.

### `IsReady(): boolean`

Returns whether the volume's own light is being drawn, for the most recent request. It is false from `Refresh`, or from a change to the box, `Spacing`, `Bounces` or `Mode`, until the volume is computed again. It is true at once on a machine that computes none. To wait: `if not volume:IsReady() then volume.Completed:Wait() end`.

### `Refresh()`

Requests that the volume be computed again. Call it after the room changes: a wall falls or a room is built.

## Events

Signals are deferred: a handler runs at the next resumption point, not
inside the call that fired the signal.

### `Completed()`

Fires when the volume finishes computing on this machine, each time `IsReady` changes from false to true. Each machine fires it at its own time, so game rules must not depend on it.
